Vs.
Munsif of First Court at Khulna & Election Tribunal and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
(c) according to rule 39 the Presiding Officer is required to seal all papers connected with the election and put them in separate packets and shall thereafter obtain the signature of the contesting candidates or their persons or polling agents on the sealed packets The Presiding Officer shall prepare the ballot paper account in Form "L". He shall then send the packets, the count-sheets prepared by him and other relevant records to the Returning Officer without delay under escort. In flagrant violation of the statutory provision the Presiding Officer of Rupsha Primary School Centre left the polling centre with the ballot boxes and all papers and concealed himself in an unknown place and he was missing till 11-30 hours on 14-8-77. He was neither found at his residence nor at the polling centre. The Election Officer-cum-Returning Officer, lodged a complaint to the police station at Khulna and Khulna P.S. Case No. 41/77 was registered under M.L.R. 17/75 and the Presiding Officer was arrested by the police. 

 (d) Similarly, the Presiding Officer of Baniakhamar Hafizia Madrassa polling centre left the centre after conclusion of the poll without depositing the ballot papers, count sheets, ballot boxes and other election materials as required under the rules. Neither he nor the election materials were found at his residence or at the centre. He disappeared and after two days he was arrested by the police on a complaint filed by the Election Officer-cum-Assistant Returning Officer, Khulna in Khulna P.S. Case No. 52 dated 16-8-77 under M.L.R. 17/75; 

 (e) the Presiding Officers of both the polling centres did not sign the form "L" as provided under rule 39, They supported the cause of the appellant by tampering with cast ballot papers and other election papers by throwing away or destroying the ballot papers in favour of the respondent and by inserting unused sealed ballot papers in the boxes of the appellant; 

 (f) consolidation of the result-sheets by the Returning Officer in form "K" has no basis as at least the two above noted Presiding Officers did neither count the ballot papers on the close of the election nor signed their respective forms nor they were available with the ballot accounts and other required papers, and as such the declaration of the result in form "K" by the Returning Officer is wholly illegal; 

 (g) 4096 votes were declared invalid and those mainly related to some particular centres. The invalid ballot papers contained double seals. Since the seals remain in the custody of the Presiding Officer, they in collusion with the appellant put the second seal on the ballot papers to render them invalid and thereby reducing the votes cast in favour of the respondent. 

 4. The election petition was contested by the appellant by submitting a written objection denying the allegations made in the election petition. At the trial 3 witnesses were examined by either side in support of their respective case. The Election Tribunal on consent of the parties and in presence of their respective Advocates opened the bags of the respective centres and found that the gunny bags of Hafizia Madrassa did not contain result-sheet and consolidated statement; and that the gunny bags of Rupsha Primary School Centre contained all the materials but there was only shortage of two votes. On consideration of the oral evidence and the materials on record the learned Munsif found that the Presiding Officers of the above named two centres violated the election rules. His decision was based on the following finding: 

 "(a) Admittedly the Returning Officer received the result of these two centres on 14-8-77 as the Presiding Officers of the said two centres were late in submission of the result sheets. On account of non-filing of result sheets and returns in accordance with rules, on the complaint of the Returning Officer they were arrested by the police and subsequently they were released. 

 (b) The Presiding Officers did not submit the result sheets and election materials to the Returning Officer. The police force was released before submitting the election materials and results to the Returning Officer. It is clear that Mr. B.N Goswami, the Presiding Officer of Rupsha Primary School Centre went to his office before submitting the election materials to the Returning Officer. It is also clear that the Presiding Officer of Baniakhamar Hafizia Madrassa Centre left for Jessore without submitting the result sheets and election materials to the Returning Officer." 

 5. On the basis of above findings the learned Munsif found that there was violation of the Election Rules 37, 38 and 39 by the Presiding Officers. With a view to verifying the allegations made in the election petition that valid votes were thrown away from ballot boxes and unused ballot papers with seals were inserted, the learned Munsif on the consent of the parties and also in presence of the respective Advocates opened the gunny bags of the two centres and found that gunny bags of Hafizia Madrassa did not contain result sheets and consolidated statement. He also found one open fresh envelope having signature of Presiding Officer Mr. Ameeruddin and all other election materials along with counter foils were also available. The gunny bag of Rupsha Primary School Centre was opened and it contained all materials and there was shortage of two votes. The learned Munsif could not rely upon the statement of the Returning Officer, because, he could not explain as to how Form "K" in respect of Hafizia Madrassa centre could be filled up when the bag itself did not contain the consolidated statement and the result-sheet. From this the learned Munsif concluded that there was violation of ejection rule 39. Presiding Officer Mr. Ameeruddin in his examination-in-chief stated that counting was over at 5 A.M. but in cross-examination he stated that the result was declared at 4 A.M. He started for Jessore at 5 A.M. after entrusting all the election materials to his Assistant Presiding Officer to submit the result, He admitted that he submitted a report to the Returning Officer on 15-8-77 with a request that the ballot boxes and election materials which E/O. refused to accept may kindly be accepted now. Mr. B.N. Goswarni, Presiding Officer of Rupsha Primary School Centre stated that counting of votes and publishing the result was completed by 2-30 A.M. He released the Police force at 2-30 A.M. He admitted that after conclusion of polls he shifted to the High School building at 5-45 P.M He admitted that with the election materials he went to his office along with some of his polling staff and on the next morning he came to the office of the Returning Officer and asked one of his polling staff to submit the election materials as he was suffering from dysentery. On consideration of the evidence the Tribunal found that there had been no declaration of results is either of the two centres. The Presiding Officers have no authority to change the centre, to go home or to office with materials, to release police force beforce submission of the election material and the result sheet. The Presiding Officers of these two centres violated the election rules as they did not observe the procedure laid down in the Election Rules. According to the Election Tribunal election of these two centres has been vitiated on account of violation of rules 37, 38 and 39. The result has, thus been materially affected on account of the irregularities already discussed above and that the election of Opposite Party No. 3 is void. Election so far as it relates to the two disputed centres is void and the appellant's election as Chairman of the Khulna Paurashava was set aside to that extent. 

 7. Petition for special leave to appeal was filed contending that there were no materials to show that there was any infraction of election rules, and even if there be any, the result of the election was materially affected thereby or that petitioner was responsible for the breach of trust; and that High Court Division was wrong in summarily dismissing the writ petition. Leave was granted to consider whether in the facts and circumstances of the case the contention can the sustained. 

 8. It has been noticed above that election in the two centres was set aside by the Election Tribunal on the ground of violation of Election Rules 37, 38 and 39. Rule 37 provides that on the conclusion of the poll in a ward the Presiding Officer shall satisfy himself and such other candidates or their election agents or polling agents as may be present at the polling station that the seals affixed to the ballot boxes are intact. It further provides that the Presiding Officer shall open the ballot box or boxes and count the entire lot of ballot papers taken out therefrom; and open the packet labelled "challenged ballot papers" and include the ballot papers therein in the court. For the purpose of counting ballot papers the rule provides necessary guidance Rule 38 deals with declaration of result. With regard to the result of the election of Chairman sub-rule (4) of rule 38 provides that when the ballot papers for Chairman contained in the ballot box or boxes have been scrutinised, the Presiding Officer shall, in the presence of the contesting candidates or their election agents or pol1ing agents count separately the valid votes cast in favour of each contesting candidates and prepare a statement in Form 'J', and with. signature of the contesting candidates or their election agents or polling agents, send the same to the Returning Officer, Sub-rule (5) of rule 38 provides that immediately on receipt of the statements in Form ‘J', the Returning Officer shall consolidate in Form 'K' the valid votes including the challenged votes cast in favour of each of the contesting candidates in each of the polling stations in the Paurashava as per statements in Form 'J' in the presence of the contesting candidates or their election agents or polling agents at the time fixed for the purpose and shall declare to be elected the contesting candidate in favour of whom the highest number of votes have been cast; and in the case of equal number of votes being recorded in favour of two or more contesting candidates, all of whom cannot be declared elected, selection shall be made from such contesting candidates by lot in such manner as the Returning Officer may deem fit and the contesting candidates thus selected shall be declared to be duly elected. Rule 39 provides the necessary instruction that the papers have to be sealed in packets. The Presiding Officer shall enclose and seal into separate packets the following papers connected with election of  commissioners or Chairman, as the case may be; 

 Sub-rule (2) of rule 39 provides that the Presiding Officer shall obtain on each packet sealed by him under sub-rule (1) the signature of such of the contesting candidate or their election agents or polling agents as may desire to sign it. Sub-rule (3) provides that Presiding Officer shall prepare a ballot paper account separately for commissioners and Chairman in Form 'L'. Sub-rule (4) provides that the Presiding Officer shall send the packets and account prepared by him and such other records as may have been received by him to the Returning Officer without delay under proper escort. 

 9. At the trial election of Chairman was challenged on various allegations, two of the allegations being that the Presiding Officers of Hafizia Madrassa Centre and Rupsha Primary School Centre under the influence of the appellant did not conduct as per election rules and violated rules 37, 38 and 39. The Presiding Officer of Rupsha Primary School Centre without counting the votes of Chairmanship election left the, centre with all election materials. The Presiding Officer of Hafizia Madrassa Centre also left the centre with all election materials without counting votes of Chairman election. It was further alleged that the two Presiding Officers did not submit the papers of the election of Chairman in consolidated form with the Returning Officer as required under the rules. It was also alleged that written complains were made to the Returning Officer reporting illegal activities of the two Presiding Officers but these were not entertained by the Returning Officer. 

 10. The Returning Officer and the two. Presiding Officers concerned were examined at the trial. Their evidence clearly supports the case of the respondent that the rules 37, 38 and 39 were not strictly complied with. The Returning Officer Md. Anwar Ali Khan (C.W. 1) stated that he sent people to these two centres in early morning on 14-8-77. The Presiding Officer B.N. Goswami along with his staff and materials were not found at the centre. The Magistrate who was deputed for the two centres reported about non-availability of the Presiding Officers. The Returning Officer could not remember whether the Presiding Officers signed the result-sheets. He stated that he received the election materials at 11-30 A.M. on 14-8-77 from Assistant Presiding Officers of these two centres. The Election Officer in consultation with the Returning Officer lodged First Information Report against the Presiding Officers concerned. He also stated that he asked about delay but the Assistant Presiding Officers kept mum. In cross-examination by the respondent he stated that he got all other results by 6 A.M. on 14-8-77 save and except the above named two centres and received the election materials at 11-30 A.M. on 14-8-77 from the respective Assistant Presiding Officers of these two centres. In cross-examination by the appellant he stated that he could not say what was declared at the spot but while B. N. Goswami handed over the result at 11-30 A.M. in his officer on 14-8-77 then none opposed the result. The Presiding Officer of Hafizia Madrassa Centre Md. Ameeruddin stated that after counting votes at the centre he left for Jessore at 5 A.M. to receive the Adviser to the President, at Jessore Airport, and when leaving the centre be entrusted all the election materials to the Assistant Presiding Officer with instruction to submit the result sheet to the Returning Officer. According to him counting was over at 5 A.M. and election papers and result sheet was submitted to the Returning Officer by the Assistant Presiding Officer at 10 A.M. on 14-8-77. He however, subsequently dated that declaration of the result was made by him at the election centre at 4 A.M. on 14-8-77 and after announcing the result he started for Jessore at 5 A M. Presiding Officer of Rupsha Primary School Centre B.N. Goswami stated that after counting of votes he declared the result at the election centre by 2-30 P.M. and then with all election materials and, election boxes came to his office as he had call of nature. Distance between his office and the polling station is about one and half miles and that of the Returning Officer is one forth mile. He admitted that after closing of voting he shifted to the High School Centre with all materials for counting votes as there was no electricity at the centre. Distance in between these two centres will be 4/5 feet. He shifted at 4-45 P.M. According to him he came to the office of the Returning Officer with election materials and he asked his Polling Assistant to submit the election materials to the Returning Officer as he could not stay there as he was suffering from dysentery and vomitting. On examination of the evidence of the three witnesses, namely the Returning Officer and the two Presiding Officers it appears that counting of votes was completed before daybreak but the result sheets along with other election materials did not reach the Returning Officer till 11-30 A. M. on 14.8.77. According to the Returning Officer he received the results of all other centres by 6 A M. on 14.8.77. He also stated that noticing unusual delay in bringing the result sheets and other election materials from Hafizia Madrassa Centre and Rupsha Primary School Centre he sent people to these centres to ascertain the position, but there was none at the centre. According to Md. Ameeruddin, the Presiding Officer of Hafizia Madrassa Centre, he after completing counting of votes and declaring the result by 4 A.M left for Jessore at 5 A.M. entrusting the election materials to his polling assistant, but there is no explanation what prevented the latter to deposit the election materials and the result sheet to the Returning Officer immediately. So far as the Presiding Officer of Rupsha Primary School Centre B.N. Goswami is concerned, he stated that after completing counting of votes and declaring results at the centre he left for his office and subsequently he came to the office of the Returning Officer. Instead of himself depositing result sheets and election materials with the Returning Officer, he asked his Assistant Presiding Officer to do it on his behalf. The Returning Officer stated that he received the result sheets and election materials from the two Assistant Presiding Officers at 11-30 A. M. on 14 8-77. In the case of Hafizia Madrassa Centre there is no explanation why the election materials and the election result were not sent to the Returning Officer before 11-30 A.M. Similarly there is no explanation why the Presiding Officer B.N Goswami, if he was actually seriously attacked with dysentery did not authorise his Assistant Presiding Officer to take the election materials and election results to the Returning Officer without any delay; distance between his office and the office of the Returning Officer is only 1/4 mile. According to him he released the police force at 2-30 A M. after finishing counting of votes and declaring the result; and then he shifted to his office. Thus from the time of shifting to his office till the election materials and election results were deposited with the office of the Returning Officer there was no police force. None of the Presiding Officers stated that according to rules signatures as provided under sub-rule (2) of rule 39 were obtained on the packets prepared and sealed by him under sub-rule (1) of rule 39. According to sub-rule (4) of rule 39 the Presiding Officer is required to send the packets and accounts prepared by him to the Returning Officer without delay under proper escort Sub-rule (4) indicates that police force is to be retained till the election materials along with result sheet are sent to the Returning Officer. In both the centres the police force was released immediately after counting of votes as admitted by the respective Presiding Officers, although their service was necessary for escorting the Presiding Officer or the Assistant Presiding Officer while taking election materials and the election results to the Returning Officer. On close examination of the evidence of the appellant and the Returning Officer it appears that according to appellant the result was finally declared by the Returning Officer at 10-30 A.M or 14-8-77. The Returning Officer no Never stated that he received the election materials at 11-30 A.M. on 14-8-77 from the Assistant Presiding Officers of these two centres. If the appellants statement is correct then the respondent's case that result of Chairmanship election was declared by the Returning Officer on the basis of statement prepared by him in Form 'K' which was prepared before receiving the result sheets of the two centres, gets supports. If the Returning Officer's statement is correct then the result of the election must have been declared sometime after 11-30 A.M. 

 11. Rules 37, 38 and 39 have been framed providing sufficient precaution to ensure fair election. Failure of compliance of these pro visions cannot be taken leniently in the absence of sufficient explanation. From the evidence shown above it does not appear that in either of the two cases there is any explanation for unusual delay in depositing the election materials and the result sheet with the Returning Officer; and there is also no explanation why the election materials and the result sheet were taken to the Returning Officer without any escort as provided under sub-rule (4) of rule 39. I am satisfied from the evidence that the Presiding Officers of the two centres completely failed to comply with the rules from closing of polls and depositing the election materials and the result sheet with the Returning Officer. 

 12. The Election Tribunal on consideration of the clear violation of the rules set aside the election held in the two centres. The learned Judges of the High Court Division rejected the writ petition with the observation that removal of the election materials from these two centres before counting of votes and declaration of election results has materially and adversely affected the sanctity of ballot boxes. The learned Judges on consideration of the facts and circumstances were of the opinion that the election result had been materially affected for non-observance of rules 37, 38 and 39 of the Paurashava Election Rules. 

 13. In an election case the decision of the Election Tribunal is final. Its decision should not be disturbed, unless it suffers from material illegality in the exercise of jurisdiction or the procedure as laid down under the rules. Evidence sufficiently shows that there was infraction of election rules, and in the absence of any explanation for the unusual delay in depositing the election materials and the result sheets with the Returning Officer, and that too without any escort, it is difficult to accept that the election was fair. When non-compliance of the mandatory rules of election is established, the person complaining non-compliance of the rules is not required to further prove responsibility in such non-compliance of the person in whose favour election result was declared. Strict compliance of the rules 37, 38 and 39 is a must for ensuring fair election. In that view of the matter the decision of the Election Tribunal should not be disturbed and the appeal is liable to be dismissed. Accordingly, I dismiss the appeal without any order as to costs. 

 Badrul Haider Chowdhury, J.—This appeal by special leave is directed against the judgment and order of the Bench of the High Court Division in Writ. Petition No. 56 of 1981. 

 14. The appellant was elected as Chairman of Khulna Paurashava and secured 40.600 votes as against, 40,265 secured by respondent No. 2 Md. Serajul Islam, his nearest rival Thereafter Serajul Islam filed an election petition (Case No. 5 of 1978) challenging the election alleging that it had been vitiated by violation of Rules 37, 38 and 39 of Paurashava Election Rules which materially affected the result of the election. He made allegation against the Presiding Officer of Rupsa Primary School Centre that the Presiding Officer removed the ballot boxes and papers and be also made allegation against the Presiding Officer of Baniakhamer Hafizia Madrassa that he left the Centre without depositing the ballot boxes and other papers. 

 15. The appellant contested the election petition by filing written objection denying all material allegations. The Election Tribunal after hearing the parties came to the conclusion that the Election Rules 37, 38 and 39 were violated and accordingly directed re-election in the aforesaid Polling Centre. This decision of the Election Tribunal was challenged by the appellant in the Writ jurisdiction. The High Court Division came to the conclusion that the finding by the Tribunal that the election materials were taken out of the said Centres before counting of votes and declaration of election result after such removal of the election materials has materially and adversely affected the sanctity of the ballot boxes and considered the election result had been materially affected for non-observance of Rules 37, 38 and 39 of the Paurashava Election Rules and therefore, up-held the decision of the Tribunal and summarily rejected the writ petition. 

 Mr. Syed Ishtiaq Ahmed placed before the Court the abstract of polling in 85 Centres which are as follows:- 

 20. In the instant case the evidence of the Returning Officer had been cited. The Returning Officer stated that there had been no allegation about malpractices in election from any Centres. He categorically denied that there had been any allegation of malpractices. He stated that he lodged a complaint against Mr. B. N. Ghoswami who was Presiding Officer in Rupsa Primary School but he stated that when Mr. B. N. Ghoswami handed over the result at 11-30 A.M on 14-8-77 then no one opposed the result. He further stated that he visited the, Polling Centre on the day of poll (13-8-77) and no one lodged any complaint. 

 22. Mr. Ameeruddin, the Presiding officer at Hafizia Madrasha centre stated that he counted the votes at the Centre and declared the result on the spot. There was no allegation of any lapse or irregularity. He stated that election papers and result sheets were submitted to Returning Officer by Assistant Presiding Officer at 10 A.M. on the following day i. e. on 14th day of August 1977 and he finished counting of votes and on the following morning, he gave out the election result. He stated that he submitted a report to Returning Officer on 15-8-77 that the counting of votes was done in presence of polling agents of the candidates. He stated that there had been no violation of election rules. 

 "That it is false that the valid votes of petitioner were thrown away from the ballot boxes by the Presiding Officer. It is also false that the Presiding Officers sealed unused ballot papers in favour of O.P. No. 3 and put the same into the ballot boxes." 

 "However from the above depositions it is Clear that Presiding Officers did not submit the result and election materials to the R/O. It is also clear that P/Officers released the police force .before submitting the result and materials. It is also clear that Mr. B.N. Ghoswami has gone to this office before submitting the materials to the R/O. It is also clear that P/Officers were late in submission of results. That it is also clear that the P/O. of Rupsa centre left the centre just after closing of the poll for High School. It is also clear that within common boundary there have been two centres for gents and ladies having separate PI Officers. It is also clear that the P/O of Hafizia Madrasha left for Jessere, without submitting the result and materials. Thus from their admitted clear facts it is crystal clear that election rules of 37, 38 and 39 were violated by P.O." 

 24. The contention has force and the appeal must be allowed. Rule 37 deals with counting of votes, Rule 38 provides for declaration of result, Rule 39 provides for sealing and packeting. The Election Tribunal has clearly erred that lapses mentioned by it are violation of rules. In one case the Presiding Officer just moved out to the adjacent building since there was no electricity in his polling station Is was the middle of August and one can easily understand the condition of these Officers in a place while performing such onerous task where there was no electricity. Naturally they would like to move to the adjacent building where electricity was available. This shifting from one place to another place definitely cannot be characterised as removal within the meaning of law laid down by this Court in 27 DLR (A.D.) 337 and further the rule laid down in 28 DLR (A.D) 51 has no manner of application. In the other case, the Presiding Officer went out to answer the call of nature. These are all post-poll affairs. These had nothing to do with the election of the candidate for Chairmanship and these lapses cannot be of such nature which may affect the result of the election. It is not the question of discretion of any Tribunal or Court which will be exercised for nullifying the decision given through democratic process. To maintain such attitude is to defeat the very purpose of law. The analysis of the election result and the polling of votes by the respective candidates clearly show that the respondent had no reason to feel aggrieved because in those two centres he had secured substantial majority. To nullify such decision by artificial reasoning claiming that the lapses had materially affected the result of the election without furnishing cogent grounds is to do violence the language of the statute. The facts and circumstances of this case do not warrant any such conclusion that infraction of election rule had materially affected the result of this election. 

 In the result, therefore, this appeal is allowed. The Orders of the Courts below are set aside and the election petition is dismissed. There will be no order as to cost. 

 ORDER OF THE COURT 

 By the majority decision the appeal is allowed. The orders of the Courts below are set aside and the erection petition is dismissed. There will be no order as to cost.
